newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Civilians report accord with Bosnian Serb generals.
newsitem.headline: Civilians report accord with Bosnian Serb generals.

text.p: Bosnian Serb political leaders said on Monday they had reached an agreement with ousted generals on transferring authority to new commanders.
There was no immediate confirmation from Bosnian Serb army officers.

Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic's office issued a statement saying she met the dismissed generals and agreed details of the transfer of power from the old general staff to the newly-appointed command.
The "handover of authority" should take place soon and was in line with Plavsic's order on November 11 to replace commander Ratko Mladic and the rest of the general staff, the statement said.
The announcement followed a meeting between Plavsic and six top generals which lasted more than seven hours.
Discussions over the weekend had ended inconclusively on Saturday.
The dispute stems from Plavsic's decision last week to dismiss General Mladic, an indicted war criminal, and the rest of his general staff -- a move the army has so far refused to recognise.
The army's highest-ranking generals attended the talks in the northern city of Banja Luka, except for Mladic and his senior aide, General Milan Gvero.
Earlier, one senior commander hinted that a compromise resolution may be imminent.
"There is always a solution to any problem. We are seeing one now," said the officer, who asked not to be named.

Plavsic met Generals Momir Talic, Novica Simic, Zdravko Tolimir, Zivomir Ninkovic and former chief of staff Manojlo Milovanovic. The newly appointed commander, General Pero Colic, also attended the meeting.
The two sides traded insults over the weekend, with Colic accusing the sacked officers of clinging to their jobs out of ambition.
"This crisis is a crisis of individuals, sickly ambitious people," Bosnian Serb television quoted Colic as saying.
Bosnian Serb media, under the control of civilian authorities, also reported that army officers had taken control of a TV transmitter on Mount Zep in eastern Bosnia last Tuesday.
The seizure prevented Serb television, based in the government seat Pale, from broadcasting to other towns in Bosnia's Serb republic.
Milovanovic lashed out at the civilian authorities in a Belgrade newspaper interview.
"The conflict between the Interior Ministry and the army of the (Bosnian) Serb republic is on the brink of an open conflict and threatens to become a genuine civil war," he said.
Serb generals loyal to Mladic, who must step down under the Dayton peace agreement, have insisted the general staff should have a say over the military's reorganisation.
They have scoffed at the new commanders as unqualified party hacks.
